subject.title: Durable Core PR 4/6: persist agent-turn front doors

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this opt-in durable SQLite control plane, including the `durable` configuration surface and authority-mode startup/ingress fail-closed behavior, as a core product contract before the stacked implementation lands?
rationale: The patch creates a broad persisted lifecycle and recovery policy across many core front doors; code review cannot determine whether this new permanent configuration and operator contract belongs in core or should be narrowed, deferred, or routed elsewhere.

options.title: Sponsor the core contract
options.body: Approve the durable runtime as a supported core feature, contingent on focused protocol proof and explicit upgrade/operator documentation.

options.title: Narrow the scope
options.body: Keep only a smaller owner-specific recovery or diagnostic seam and remove the cross-front-door durable runtime contract from this stack.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Pause this stacked feature until maintainers define the desired persistence, recovery, and support boundary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the core contract
recommendation.body: Approve the durable runtime as a supported core feature, contingent on focused protocol proof and explicit upgrade/operator documentation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses the existing Gateway, agent, session, and state persistence ownership boundaries, and no single current-main history owner could be verified in this read-only review.
